summary.text: A 23-year-old woman with no known medical illness was referred with a two-month history of throbbing headache with palpitations, sweating, nausea and vomiting. Examination was unremarkable apart from acanthosis nigricans and her blood pressure was 178/97 mmHg. Plasma and urine metanephrines and normetanephrines were markedly elevated.

Contrast CT showed bilateral adrenal masses, MIBG scintigraphy showed bilateral functioning pheochromocytoma, and thyroid ultrasound showed a right hypoechoic lesion whose fine-needle aspiration revealed medullary thyroid carcinoma. She was diagnosed with MEN 2 with medullary thyroid cancer and bilateral pheochromocytoma; RET testing was later positive and family members were advised to undergo screening.

After preparation with phenoxybenzamine and carvedilol she underwent bilateral laparoscopic retroperitoneal adrenalectomy, with an uneventful postoperative course. Two months later she underwent total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection and was discharged on thyroxine. Histopathology showed bilateral pheochromocytomas and bilateral multifocal medullary thyroid carcinoma.

After being lost to follow-up during the COVID-19 pandemic she returned in 2021 with headache and elevated blood pressure, and imaging and laboratory tests indicated recurrent pheochromocytoma at the left adrenal bed. She refused CRS and HIPEC, underwent en bloc resection in 2023, was managed as malignant recurrent disease with adjuvant iodine-MIBG radiotherapy, and a CT in September 2024 was negative for recurrence.
